title: CATBOY CAUGHT RED-PAWED WITH HAND STUCK IN CERAMIC HEN COOKIE JAR
headline: CATBOY CAUGHT RED-PAWED WITH HAND STUCK IN CERAMIC HEN COOKIE JAR
summary: A Northport family awoke to a faint clinking at 1:58 AM and found the elusive Catboy standing in their kitchen with his hand wedged inside a ceramic hen-shaped cookie jar, refusing to let go of the oatmeal cookie that was keeping it there.
commentary:
Folklore has warned us for generations about getting caught with your hand in the cookie jar. Nobody expected it to be literal, and nobody expected the hand to belong to a cryptid. Yet at 1:58 AM on Tuesday, the Hollis family of Northport stepped into their kitchen to find Catboy lit only by the open refrigerator, his arm buried to the wrist in Henrietta, the family's beloved ceramic hen.

According to the nanny-cam footage, the problem was never the jar. The problem was the cookie. Catboy had a firm grip on an oatmeal raisin and would not release it, making his fist too wide to exit the hen's neck. For eleven minutes he simply stood there, ears flat, tail swishing, negotiating with physics.

Darlene Hollis, still in her bathrobe, described the standoff. "He looked at me like I was the one who'd broken in. I said, honey, just let go of the cookie, and he looked so betrayed. So I buttered the rim with margarine and out he slid, cookie and all." Catboy reportedly bowed, cookie in hand, and left through the doggie door.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the incident a 9.1/10 on the Weird-o-Meter, deducting points only because the jar survived without a chip. Henrietta has since been moved to a higher shelf. Count your cookies, lock your pantry, and learn to let go of what's holding you back.
image_prompt: Grainy desaturated nanny-cam still from a high corner of a dim suburban kitchen lit only by an open refrigerator. Catboy in an oversized grey hoodie and jeans stands at the counter with his arm stuck wrist-deep in a white ceramic hen-shaped cookie jar, ears flat and tail puffed, while a woman in a bathrobe stares from the doorway. Green overlay text reads "01:58 AM  HOLLIS KITCHEN CAM 2".

title: CATBOY WINS BLUE RIBBON AT COUNTY FAIR CAT SHOW, JUDGES DEEPLY CONFLICTED
headline: CATBOY WINS BLUE RIBBON AT COUNTY FAIR CAT SHOW, JUDGES DEEPLY CONFLICTED
summary: Judges at a harvest fair outside Andalusia awarded Best in Show in the household cat division to an entrant who arrived without an owner, sat perfectly still on the judging table, and was, by most accounts, a young man in a hoodie.
commentary:
The household cat division is the quietest tent at any county fair. While the pig races thunder and the funnel cakes sizzle, a row of judges inspects tabbies and Siamese with the gravity of a supreme court. At the Tri-County Harvest Fair outside Andalusia this weekend, that gravity met its match.

Entrant number 27 arrived at 8:15 PM with no owner, no carrier, and no paperwork. He hopped onto the judging table, sat with his tail wrapped neatly around his sneakers, and blinked slowly at each judge in turn. When the head judge checked his ears, he allowed it, then purred so loudly that a Persian two tables down began purring in solidarity.

Head judge Mavis Whitlock stands by the ruling. "The rulebook says household cat. He's clearly been in somebody's household, because he had cookie crumbs on his hoodie. Glossy coat, flawless posture, and regulation ears. I sleep just fine at night." Whitlock confirmed that several cat owners have filed formal complaints.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the win an 8.5/10, the first Catboy sighting ever to produce an official ribbon. He reportedly pinned it to his hoodie, ate one corn dog, and vanished behind the Tilt-A-Whirl. Brush your cats, read your rulebooks, and check every entrant's paperwork.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a county fair show tent at evening, string lights overhead and a glowing Ferris wheel visible through the open flap. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, and an oversized grey hoodie sits primly on a judging table among cats in carriers, his fluffy blue tail wrapped around his sneakers, as a stern judge with a clipboard pins a big blue Best in Show ribbon to his hoodie.

title: CATBOY LAUNCHES OVERNIGHT APOLOGY TOUR, RETURNS BORROWED ITEMS ACROSS TUSCALOOSA COUNTY
headline: CATBOY LAUNCHES OVERNIGHT APOLOGY TOUR, RETURNS BORROWED ITEMS ACROSS TUSCALOOSA COUNTY
summary: Residents across Tuscaloosa County woke this week to find long-missing household items returned to their doorsteps overnight, including a garden gnome, a ball of yarn, and one very familiar oatmeal cookie, each accompanied by a crayon note bearing a single misspelled word.
commentary:
Every cryptid has a reputation to maintain, and lately Catboy's has taken a few dings. A lifted cookie here, a borrowed dryer sheet there. But this week the elusive figure apparently decided to make things right, and he did it the way a cat would: silently, at night, and with each item placed exactly where you would trip over it.

Between Monday and Thursday, at least seventeen households from Northport to Coker reported returns. A ball of yellow yarn missing since 2019. A welcome mat that vanished from a porch in Brookwood. A single fuzzy slipper whose partner had long since given up hope. A garden gnome, returned with a fresh coat of paint on its little hat. Each came with a note in blue crayon reading only sory, with one r.

Darlene Hollis of Northport, whose kitchen hosted the infamous cookie jar incident, received a napkin-wrapped oatmeal raisin cookie. "That's the cookie. The same one. He never ate it. I guess he held onto it all this time out of guilt. I put it back in the hen. I couldn't bring myself to do anything else."

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the tour a 9.6/10, calling remorse an unprecedented development in cryptid behavior and noting that Batboy never apologized for anything. Residents are encouraged to check their porches and their hearts. Forgive freely, spell generously, and leave the porch light on.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a moonlit suburban front porch with a glowing porch light and moths. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, a long fluffy blue tail, and an oversized grey hoodie tiptoes on the steps as he gently sets down a napkin-wrapped cookie beside a freshly painted garden gnome, a ball of yellow yarn, and a single fuzzy slipper, with a small crayon note reading "sory" propped against them.

title: CATBOY BUILDS NEST OF DRYER SHEETS IN TUSCALOOSA LAUNDROMAT AT 3:12 AM
headline: CATBOY BUILDS NEST OF DRYER SHEETS IN TUSCALOOSA LAUNDROMAT AT 3:12 AM
summary: Security footage from a Tuscaloosa laundromat shows Catboy pulling an entire box of Mountain Breeze Dryer Sheets into a fluffy pile at 3:12 AM, then curling up in it and sleeping until the spin cycle ended.
commentary:
There are two kinds of people in a laundromat at 3:12 AM: those running from their problems and those running a heavy-duty cycle. On Thursday, the Suds City Coin Laundry on 15th Street hosted a third kind. Grainy footage shows Catboy padding in through the automatic door, ears swiveling at the hum of the machines, and heading straight for a forgotten box of Mountain Breeze Dryer Sheets.

What followed was methodical. One sheet at a time, he drew them out, sniffed each with grave concentration, and arranged them into a soft white mound on the folding table. He then turned three slow circles and lay down, tail curled over his nose, in what experts can only describe as a fabric-softened nest.

Night attendant Loretta Biggs discovered him when the dryers buzzed. "Smelled like a spring meadow in there. He woke up, stretched about a foot longer than a person ought to, and walked out with one sheet stuck to his hood. Didn't even ask for his quarters back, on account of he never put any in." Her own laundry, she noted, came out static-free for the first time in years.

Dr. Patricia Meowton gave the sighting an 8.7/10, citing the circling behavior as textbook feline. Suds City has since stocked extra boxes, just in case. Fold your sheets, clean your lint traps, and leave a little softness out for the night shift.
image_prompt: Grainy desaturated security-camera still of a fluorescent-lit coin laundromat at night with rows of front-loading dryers. Catboy in an oversized grey hoodie lies curled on a folding table inside a fluffy mound of white dryer sheets, tail wrapped over his nose, an open dryer-sheet box tipped beside him. Green overlay text reads "03:12 AM  SUDS CITY COIN LAUNDRY CAM 1".

title: CATBOY ATTENDS CHURCH POTLUCK, EATS ONLY THE TUNA CASSEROLE
headline: CATBOY ATTENDS CHURCH POTLUCK, EATS ONLY THE TUNA CASSEROLE
summary: Members of a small Selma congregation say a shy young man in a grey hoodie joined their Wednesday night potluck, walked past forty-one other dishes, and quietly finished every last bite of the tuna noodle casserole.
commentary:
Every church potluck has a hierarchy. The fried chicken goes first, the banana pudding second, and the mystery gelatin salad goes home exactly as it came. At Shady Grove Fellowship in Selma on Wednesday night, that hierarchy was overturned by a guest nobody remembers inviting.

He arrived just after the blessing, hood up and tail tucked into his jeans, though not very successfully. Witnesses say he walked the length of the fellowship hall slowly, sniffing each dish like a judge at the county fair, before stopping at a dented casserole pan near the end of the table. He pulled up a folding chair, picked up the serving spoon, and did not look up again for twenty minutes.

The casserole belonged to Ida Mae Gaines, eighty-three, who has brought the same dish to every potluck since 1971. "Fifty-five years I've been bringing that tuna and nobody ever went back for seconds. That child went back for fifths. He licked the spoon and said thank you real quiet. I don't care if he's a cryptid. He's got taste."

Pastor Leon Burks declined to speculate on the visitor's nature, but noted that the church's resident barn cat has followed Mrs. Gaines's empty pan around ever since. The next potluck is the first Wednesday of the month, and she is bringing two pans. Bless the cooks, save a plate, and always make room for the stranger.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a warmly lit small-town church fellowship hall in the evening, long folding tables crowded with casseroles, fried chicken, and banana pudding. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, and an oversized grey hoodie sits on a folding chair blissfully eating straight from a dented pan of tuna noodle casserole, his fluffy blue tail escaping from his jeans, while a delighted elderly woman in a church hat beams beside him.

title: CATBOY DODGES EVERY SINGLE PUDDLE ON FLOODED GULFPORT BOARDWALK
headline: CATBOY DODGES EVERY SINGLE PUDDLE ON FLOODED GULFPORT BOARDWALK
summary: During a midnight downpour on the Gulfport waterfront, Catboy was seen leaping, twisting, and tiptoeing across a flooded boardwalk without touching a single drop of standing water, then shaking himself off under an awning anyway.
commentary:
Another storm rolled in off the Gulf this week, dumping three inches of rain on the Mississippi coast. While residents bailed out carports and fished patio furniture out of hedges, one figure on the Gulfport boardwalk treated the downpour as an obstacle course, and he was winning.

Shortly after midnight, a dock worker's phone captured Catboy crossing nearly a quarter mile of boardwalk where puddles stretched like small lakes. He hopped from dry plank to dry plank, vaulted a park bench, walked a railing like a tightrope, and sailed clean over a dozing pelican, which did not wake up, before landing on the one dry square of sidewalk left in Harrison County.

Shrimper Tommy Ladner, who was tying down his boat, forgot about the storm entirely. "I've lived here sixty years and I've stepped in every puddle God ever made. That boy didn't step in one. Then he gets under the awning dry as a biscuit and shakes himself off like a wet dog anyway. Out of principle, I reckon."

Dr. Patricia Meowton gave the sighting an 8.9/10, calling the unnecessary shake a fascinating ritual of pure habit. Local meteorologists declined to comment, reportedly still sore about the bicycle incident. Stay dry, stay off the railings, and let the pelicans sleep.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a rain-lashed wooden boardwalk at night along the Gulf, streetlamps reflecting in wide puddles. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, a long fluffy blue tail, and an oversized grey hoodie leaps gracefully mid-air between dry planks over a sleeping pelican, rain streaking around him, while a shrimper in a yellow slicker watches from a docked boat.

title: CATBOY PAYS A QUARTER FOR EMPTY CARDBOARD BOX, SITS IN IT FOR SIX HOURS
headline: CATBOY PAYS A QUARTER FOR EMPTY CARDBOARD BOX, SITS IN IT FOR SIX HOURS
summary: The hottest item at a Fairhope yard sale turned out to be the box a microwave came in, after Catboy bought it for twenty-five cents, climbed inside, and refused to leave the driveway until well after the sale ended.
commentary:
The early bird gets the worm, and at a Southern yard sale the early bird usually gets the good cast iron. At the Pruitt family's driveway sale in Fairhope on Saturday, the early bird arrived at 6:02 AM, ignored the cast iron, the lamps, and a perfectly good exercise bike, and made a beeline for a stack of flattened boxes marked twenty-five cents.

He selected a microwave box, unfolded it with great care, placed a single quarter on the card table, and climbed in. Then he sat, knees tucked, ears just visible above the flaps, as shoppers came and went around him. Several people tried to buy the exercise bike. Nobody tried to buy the box. It was very clearly taken.

Seller Gloria Pruitt said the visitor caused no trouble at all. "I've sold that exercise bike at four yard sales and somehow it keeps coming back. That boy spent one quarter and got the best deal of the morning. Six hours he sat there. Folks started leaving him lemonade like an offering." By 1 PM the box had collected two lemonades, a granola bar, and a child's crayon drawing of a cat.

At sunset, Pruitt turned to carry in the folding tables, and when she looked back the box was empty except for the drawing, neatly folded. The exercise bike, once again, remains unsold. Shop early, haggle kindly, and never throw away a good box.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a sunny suburban driveway yard sale under live oaks with Spanish moss, folding tables of lamps and cast iron and an unloved exercise bike. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, and an oversized grey hoodie sits contentedly inside an open cardboard box, only his ears and eyes peeking over the flaps, his fluffy blue tail curling out one side, surrounded by small cups of lemonade left by shoppers.

title: POWDERED SUGAR PAW PRINTS LEAD TO CATBOY AT ALL-NIGHT NEW ORLEANS CAFE
headline: POWDERED SUGAR PAW PRINTS LEAD TO CATBOY AT ALL-NIGHT NEW ORLEANS CAFE
summary: Staff at an all-night French Quarter cafe followed a trail of powdered-sugar prints from the pastry case to a back booth, where security footage shows Catboy contentedly eating a beignet the size of his head at 4:18 AM.
commentary:
New Orleans has its share of ghosts, vampires, and riverboat legends. It now appears to have a cryptid with a sweet tooth. At 4:18 AM Tuesday, the overnight crew at Cafe Bonne Nuit on Decatur Street noticed something odd on the black-and-white tile floor: a winding trail of powdered sugar. Some prints were sneaker soles. Others, on the countertops, were small hands with suspiciously rounded fingertips.

The trail led past the register, across the pastry case, along the top of the jukebox, and into the last booth by the window, where the camera shows Catboy sitting cross-legged with a beignet roughly the size of his head. Each bite released a small cloud of sugar. By the third bite he was coated from ears to tail, like a very surprised snowman.

Night baker Antoine Broussard could not bring himself to interrupt. "Thirty years I've been frying beignets and I never saw anybody enjoy one like that. Sugar on his ears, sugar on his tail, sugar on the ceiling somehow. Then he licked his fingers clean, one at a time, and left a bottle cap on the table." Broussard added that the jukebox has played nothing but zydeco since.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting an 8.1/10, marking the first confirmed Catboy appearance in Louisiana and noting that his bottle-cap tipping habit has now crossed state lines. Bonne Nuit staff plan to leave a warm cafe au lait out nightly. Sweep your floors, sugar your coffee, and keep your cats indoors.
image_prompt: Grainy desaturated security-camera still of a small all-night cafe with black-and-white checkered tile and a glowing jukebox. title: CATBOY KEEPS PERFECT TIME WITH HIS TAIL AT MIDNIGHT MEMPHIS BLUES JAM
headline: CATBOY KEEPS PERFECT TIME WITH HIS TAIL AT MIDNIGHT MEMPHIS BLUES JAM
summary: Musicians at a late-night street jam in Memphis, Tennessee, say Catboy sat on a milk crate for three hours keeping flawless rhythm with his tail, and that the band has never sounded tighter.
commentary:
Memphis is a city built on rhythm, and a good drummer there is worth his weight in barbecue. So when the regular drummer for a Thursday midnight blues jam outside a shuttered record shop failed to show, the band feared the worst. Then somebody noticed the kid on the milk crate.

He had wandered up around 11:50 PM, hood up, and settled onto an upturned crate beside the trumpet player. As the first song began, his tail started moving: a slow sway on the shuffle, a sharp flick on the backbeat, a full loop-the-loop on the turnaround. Within minutes the whole band was watching his tail instead of each other, and nobody missed a chord change all night.

Harmonica player Clarence Woodbine, who has worked that corner for thirty-one years, called it the tightest set of his life. "I've played with drummers who couldn't count to four with a calculator. That boy counted with his tail and never dropped a beat. Play it slow and his ears went down. Play it fast and they shot straight up. You can't teach that. That's soul."

The band reports that the tip jar contained, along with the usual dollar bills, one unopened sardine tin and a single bottle cap. The regular drummer has been told, kindly, that his position is under review. Keep the blues alive, Memphis, and always save a crate for the rhythm section.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a gritty Memphis street corner at midnight, neon signs and a shuttered record shop glowing behind a small blues band with a harmonica player, a trumpeter, and a guitarist. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, and an oversized grey hoodie sits on an upturned milk crate, eyes half closed in the groove, his long fluffy blue tail swinging in a rhythmic arc while the musicians watch it to keep time.

title: CATBOY CHASES LASER POINTER THROUGH TUSCALOOSA CITY COUNCIL BUDGET MEETING
headline: CATBOY CHASES LASER POINTER THROUGH TUSCALOOSA CITY COUNCIL BUDGET MEETING
summary: A late-night budget hearing ground to a halt when a staffer's laser pointer drew Catboy out from behind the chamber curtain, and the livestream camera caught him pouncing after the red dot across slides about sewer bonds.
commentary:
Municipal budget meetings rarely make the news, and they almost never make the cryptid news. But at 11:47 PM Tuesday, three hours into a hearing on the city drainage plan, a Tuscaloosa finance staffer clicked on a laser pointer to highlight a pie chart. The pie chart did not survive.

The chamber's livestream camera shows a blur emerging from behind the velvet curtain at the back of the dais. Catboy, hoodie flapping, launched himself at the projection screen, swatting at the red dot as it skittered across sewer bond projections, a bar graph on pothole repair, and finally the city seal. The staffer, frozen in shock, kept the pointer moving for nearly six minutes.

Council member Gerald Pike, a longtime skeptic of all things cryptid, insisted afterward that he saw nothing unusual. "What I observed was a young man with an extremely enthusiastic interest in infrastructure spending. Frankly, that is more public engagement than we usually get. I would like to see that energy at the zoning hearings." Pike then asked that the footage be deleted. It has been viewed forty thousand times.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the incident an 8.8/10, noting that the drainage budget passed unanimously moments after Catboy left, possibly because nobody could remember what they had been arguing about. Attend your local meetings, point responsibly, and keep your pie charts out of reach.

title: CATBOY CHASES HALFTIME SPOTLIGHT ACROSS FIFTY-YARD LINE AT OPELIKA FOOTBALL GAME
headline: CATBOY CHASES HALFTIME SPOTLIGHT ACROSS FIFTY-YARD LINE AT OPELIKA FOOTBALL GAME
summary: Thousands of fans at a Friday night high school football game in Opelika watched Catboy bound onto the field at halftime and chase the band's roving spotlight from end zone to end zone, earning a standing ovation and an honorary spot in the drumline.
commentary:
In the South, Friday night football is not a sport. It is a way of life with a concession stand. So when the halftime show at Pinewood Memorial Field in Opelika was interrupted last week, a hush fell over five thousand fans that has not been heard since the stadium lights failed in 1998.

The Pinewood High Marching Panthers were mid-formation when the lighting crew swept a single spotlight across the turf. Out of the visitor bleachers sprang Catboy, ears forward, pouncing after the circle of light as it zigzagged across the field. The operator, sensing history, kept it moving. Catboy dove, rolled, and skidded straight through the drumline, which never missed a beat.

Band director Marvin Ellis called it the best show in school history. "We practiced that routine for six weeks and that young man upstaged us in four minutes. The tuba section wants him at every game. I told them he's not enrolled. They told me rules are rules, but rhythm is rhythm." The Panther mascot was later seen high-fiving Catboy at the forty-yard line.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the event a 9.2/10 on the Weird-o-Meter, noting it was the first Catboy sighting with a live drumline soundtrack. The Panthers won 21 to 14, though few fans could tell you who scored. Go team, go band, and keep that spotlight moving.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a packed small-town high school football stadium at night under blazing stadium lights, a marching band in maroon uniforms frozen mid-formation on the field. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, a long fluffy blue tail, and an oversized grey hoodie leaps in a dramatic pounce at a bright circle of spotlight on the fifty-yard line, while the crowd in the bleachers rises to its feet cheering.

title: CATBOY BOWLS PERFECT GAME USING ONLY HIS TAIL AT MOBILE BOWLING ALLEY
headline: CATBOY BOWLS PERFECT GAME USING ONLY HIS TAIL AT MOBILE BOWLING ALLEY
summary: Late-night bowlers in Mobile watched Catboy roll twelve consecutive strikes by swinging the ball with his long fluffy tail, never once putting on rental shoes.
commentary:
Cosmic bowling night at Bay Strike Lanes usually means black lights, fog machines, and somebody's uncle doing the moonwalk on lane six. On Friday it meant history. Shortly after midnight, Catboy emerged from the fog, selected a glittering eight-pound ball, and wrapped his tail around it like a fluffy slingshot.

Twelve frames. Twelve strikes. Each roll began with a dramatic tail wind-up and ended with pins scattering like startled pigeons. Between frames he sat on the ball return, warming his hands over the air blower and ignoring the scoreboard entirely, as if perfection is simply what happens when you do not care.

League veteran Earl Tidwell, who has bowled at Bay Strike since 1979, was on lane seven. "Forty-five years I've been chasing a three hundred. That young fella did it with a tail. I'm not mad. I'm just going to go sit in my truck for a while." Tidwell later conceded the form was, technically, flawless.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the spectacle a 9.3/10 on the Weird-o-Meter, noting that bowling shoes were never offered and never required. Lane eight has been roped off as a shrine. Mind your gutters, pick up your spares, and never underestimate the new kid on the next lane.
image_prompt: Polished cinematic anime illustration of a neon-lit bowling alley under purple black lights and drifting fog. Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears, and an oversized grey hoodie swings a glittering bowling ball forward with his long fluffy blue tail, pins exploding at the end of the lane. An astonished older bowler in a league shirt gapes from the next lane.

title: CATBOY KNOCKS ITEMS OFF SHELF ONE BY ONE WHILE STARING INTO SECURITY CAMERA
headline: CATBOY KNOCKS ITEMS OFF SHELF ONE BY ONE WHILE STARING INTO SECURITY CAMERA
summary: Overnight footage from a 24-hour supercenter in Gadsden shows Catboy holding unbroken eye contact with a security camera while slowly nudging forty-two items off a shelf, then carefully putting every single one of them back.
commentary:
Anyone who has lived with a cat knows the look. The slow, deliberate stare. The single hand extended toward your coffee mug. The pause, as if to ask whether you plan to do anything about it. On Wednesday at 3:58 AM, the aisle seven camera at the MegaSave 24-Hour Supercenter in Gadsden received that look, and it received it for twenty-two minutes.

The footage shows Catboy standing before a shelf of Sunny Valley canned peaches, eyes locked on the lens. Without looking down, he nudges a can toward the edge. It wobbles. It falls. He does not blink. He repeats this forty-two times, working his way through the peaches, a tower of paper towels, and a seasonal display of plush pumpkin pillows, never once breaking eye contact.

Then, according to overnight stocker Ruthie Calloway, he did something no cat in history has done. "He put them all back. Every can, every roll, every pumpkin, labels facing out, neater than I do it. Then he looked up at the camera one more time like, you saw that, right? And off he went toward the pet aisle." Calloway says aisle seven has never looked so tidy.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the episode a 9.5/10, calling it a historic first in feline restraint and possibly a sign of personal growth. Store management has formally invited him back for inventory week. Stare boldly, push gently, and always clean up after yourself.

title: CATBOY SPOTTED FAR FROM HOME ON FOGGY MAINE FISHING PIER
headline: CATBOY SPOTTED FAR FROM HOME ON FOGGY MAINE FISHING PIER
summary: Lobstermen in Portland, Maine, were startled at dawn to find a shivering Catboy at the end of their pier in a knit cap with ear holes, gazing longingly at the day's catch, in what experts are calling his northernmost sighting yet.
commentary:
Catboy is a creature of the humid South, of sweet tea evenings and Slurpee nights. So the cryptid community was stunned this week when credible reports surfaced from the docks of Portland, Maine, roughly thirteen hundred miles from the nearest Tuscaloosa 7-Eleven, give or take a few gas stations.

At 5:20 AM, as fog rolled off the bay, the crew of the lobster boat Mary Ellen returned to find a slim figure at the end of Pier Nine, knees pulled into his oversized hoodie, wearing a knit cap with two holes cut out for the ears. He did not approach. He simply watched each crate come ashore with the quiet intensity of someone reading a love letter.

Captain Ezra Tibbetts said the crew took pity on him. "Kid looked like a wet mitten. We don't give lobster away, not to anybody. But my deckhand tossed him a sardine from the bait bucket and he caught it in midair, ate it, and nodded at us like we'd shaken on a deal. Then the fog came in and he was gone." The crew has since named the pier's resident gull after him, to the gull's annoyance.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting a 9.8/10, citing the extreme distance and the custom ear holes. How he traveled north remains a mystery, though a long-haul trucker in Virginia has come forward about a silent rider who slept the whole way curled on the dashboard. Bundle up, New England, and keep a sardine in your pocket.

Catboy with messy blue hair, blue cat ears poking through holes in a knit cap, a long fluffy blue tail, and an oversized grey hoodie sits hugging his knees at the end of the pier, catching a tossed silver sardine in midair as a bearded fisherman in orange oilskins looks on.

title: WEIRD-O-METER REVISED: DR. MEOWTON RAISES ORIGINAL 7-ELEVEN SIGHTING TO 9.9
headline: WEIRD-O-METER REVISED: DR. MEOWTON RAISES ORIGINAL 7-ELEVEN SIGHTING TO 9.9
summary: Cryptid expert Dr. Patricia Meowton has officially raised her rating of the original 2:47 AM Tuscaloosa 7-Eleven sighting after enhanced footage revealed Catboy refilled his blue-raspberry Slurpee four separate times.
commentary:
In the cryptid sciences, no rating is ever truly final. This week, Dr. Patricia Meowton did something she has done only once before in her career, the last time over the 1992 Batboy precedent: she reopened a case. The subject was the sighting that started it all, the 2:47 AM visit to a Tuscaloosa 7-Eleven and the now-legendary blue-raspberry Slurpee incident.

The revision follows a frame-by-frame enhancement of the store's security tape by a volunteer team of retired TV repairmen. Their analysis shows that Catboy did not fill one Slurpee, as originally reported, but four, topping off the same cup each time after sipping it down to a precise line. In the final frames, his tongue is visibly, unmistakably blue.

Dr. Meowton presented the findings at a press conference in the store's parking lot. "We underestimated him. Four refills on a single cup is not hunger, it is strategy. Add the brain freeze he clearly suffered at 2:49 and refused to acknowledge, and the science leaves me no choice. The new rating is 9.9 out of 10." She declined to say what a perfect ten would require.

Store management confirmed the refill policy was technically honored. A Tuscaloosa County commissioner who asked not to be named dismissed the revision as grandstanding, though he was seen buying a blue-raspberry Slurpee shortly afterward. Science marches on, and so does Catboy. Keep your tapes, your cups, and your minds wide open.

title: CATBOY CONQUERS CLAW MACHINE, WINS EVERY PLUSH FISH IN HUNTSVILLE ARCADE
headline: CATBOY CONQUERS CLAW MACHINE, WINS EVERY PLUSH FISH IN HUNTSVILLE ARCADE
summary: A 24-hour arcade in Huntsville is short one claw machine's worth of plush fish after Catboy spent the early morning hours winning them one by one, leaving every stuffed animal that was not a fish untouched.
commentary:
Rocket City Fun Zone advertises itself as open 24 hours for the serious gamer. It did not anticipate the competition. At 2:31 AM Saturday, a security camera above the skee-ball lanes recorded Catboy standing before the Mega Grabber 3000, eyes wide, tail twitching like a metronome.

Claw machines are notorious for their weak grip and crushing disappointments. Catboy appears to have been unaware of this. Over forty minutes he extracted fourteen plush fish, a plush shrimp, and a felt sardine of unknown origin. The bears, the unicorns, and one smug-looking avocado were passed over with visible contempt.

Night manager Corey Dunlap, who once spent sixty dollars failing to win a stuffed duck, watched in awe. "I have never seen that claw grip anything in my life. He'd just stare at it real hard and the claw would hold on like it owed him money. Then he hugged the whole pile and left out the back." No tokens were reported missing, raising questions about how he paid.

Dr. Patricia Meowton awarded the sighting an 8.2/10, adding that cryptid telekinesis remains unconfirmed but deeply plausible. The machine has been restocked with fish, and the avocado remains unclaimed. Game on, Huntsville, and guard your prize tickets.

title: CATBOY ORDERS AT BAMA BURGER BARN DRIVE-THROUGH WITHOUT A CAR
headline: CATBOY ORDERS AT BAMA BURGER BARN DRIVE-THROUGH WITHOUT A CAR
summary: Overnight staff at a Prattville Bama Burger Barn say Catboy walked up to the drive-through speaker at 1:33 AM, meowed his order, and waited patiently in line between two idling pickup trucks.
commentary:
Drive-through policy at most burger joints is firm: no walk-ups. At the Bama Burger Barn on Highway 31 in Prattville, that policy was tested at 1:33 AM Sunday, when the lane camera captured a lone pedestrian in the drive-through, hood up, tail curled patiently behind him, sandwiched between two pickup trucks.

When he reached the speaker, he leaned in, cleared his throat, and delivered his order in what employees describe as a single, polite, extremely long meow. The pickup behind him did not honk. The pickup in front of him, according to the footage, paid for his meal and drove off without a word, which staff believe may be the most Southern thing ever recorded.

Headset operator Tavon Rucker did his best to interpret. "I heard that meow and I just knew in my heart he wanted a fish sandwich, no bun, extra tartar, and a small cup of milk. We don't sell milk by the cup. I gave him one anyway. Some orders you don't argue with." At the window, Catboy accepted the bag with both hands and bowed.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting a 7.2/10, calling the bow consistent with previous accounts of Catboy etiquette. Bama Burger Barn has declined to change its walk-up policy but has quietly added milk to the overnight menu. Pull forward, check your bag, and pay it forward when you can.

title: CATBOY SKIPS THE SOAP, STAYS FOR THE BLOW-DRY AT MONTGOMERY CAR WASH
headline: CATBOY SKIPS THE SOAP, STAYS FOR THE BLOW-DRY AT MONTGOMERY CAR WASH
summary: A Montgomery car wash camera caught Catboy tiptoeing around every sprayer, brush, and soap curtain in the tunnel at 1:44 AM, only to stand blissfully beneath the giant air blowers for a full twenty minutes.
commentary:
Cats are famously opposed to water, and it seems cryptid cats are no exception. At 1:44 AM Wednesday, the tunnel camera at Shine Time Express Wash on the Atlanta Highway recorded Catboy entering through the exit, which is the first sign you are dealing with a professional.

He moved through the tunnel with ninja precision, ducking under the triple-foam curtain, hopping over the wheel rail, and contorting around the spinning brushes without collecting a single bubble. Then he reached the blowers. There, in the roaring wind, he simply stood, eyes closed, hoodie rippling, hair blown back into a magnificent mohawk.

Owner Raymond Pugh reviewed the footage the next morning. "Twenty minutes he stood there. He ran up about four dollars in electricity, and I'd charge him, but I've never seen a customer that happy. He looked like a dog with its head out a car window, except a cat, except a boy." Pugh has declined to file a report.

Dr. Patricia Meowton assigned the sighting a 7.4/10, deducting points for the lack of hot wax. Shine Time has since posted a small sign by the vacuums offering free blow-drys to any customer with a tail. Drive clean, tip your attendants, and always check the tunnel for ears.

title: CATBOY FALLS ASLEEP ON OPEN ENCYCLOPEDIA IN 24-HOUR CAMPUS LIBRARY
headline: CATBOY FALLS ASLEEP ON OPEN ENCYCLOPEDIA IN 24-HOUR CAMPUS LIBRARY
summary: Finals-week students at a 24-hour Auburn campus library discovered Catboy sound asleep across an old encyclopedia, cheek pressed to the entry on fish, purring loudly enough to rattle the study carrels.
commentary:
Finals week turns any college library into a nocturnal habitat of energy drinks, highlighters, and quiet despair. At the Magnolia Hall Learning Commons in Auburn, which stays open around the clock during exams, the habitat gained a new species at 3:40 AM Monday.

Students on the fourth floor first noticed a low rumble they assumed was the ventilation. It was not the ventilation. Tucked beneath a green desk lamp, Catboy lay curled across an open volume of a 1987 encyclopedia, cheek pressed firmly against the entry on fish, tail draped over a stack of chemistry textbooks.

Sophomore Kaylee Strand, cramming for organic chemistry, took the lone photograph. "Nobody wanted to wake him. Somebody made a little sign that said quiet please, cryptid sleeping, and we all just studied around him. Honestly, it was the most peaceful finals night of my life, and I got a B-plus." The photo has since been shared across campus hundreds of times.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting an 8.0/10, praising his choice of reading material. By sunrise, only a warm spot and a few stray blue hairs remained, and library staff report the encyclopedia volume is now mysteriously checked out. Study hard, nap where you can, and return your books on time.

title: CATBOY DIRECTS ELEMENTARY CARPOOL LINE WITH TAIL, CUTS WAIT TIME IN HALF
headline: CATBOY DIRECTS ELEMENTARY CARPOOL LINE WITH TAIL, CUTS WAIT TIME IN HALF
summary: Parents at a Vestavia Hills elementary school say the afternoon pickup line, normally a forty-minute ordeal, moved in record time on Thursday after a figure in a grey hoodie appeared at the curb and began waving cars forward with a long fluffy tail.
commentary:
Ask any parent and they will tell you the school pickup line is the true final boss of modern life. At Cedar Ridge Elementary in Vestavia Hills, the line routinely snakes past the church, around the dentist's office, and halfway to the interstate. On Thursday afternoon, it cleared in nineteen minutes.

The reason, according to dozens of parents, was standing on the curb by the cafeteria doors. Catboy, wearing an orange safety vest over his hoodie, signaled each car forward with sweeping tail motions, seemed to know which child belonged to which minivan before anyone said a name, and halted all traffic for a family of crossing ducks with one raised hand.

Mother of three Brittany Sowell said the experience changed her. "I've done that line for six years. I've eaten whole meals in that line. I've filed my taxes in that line. Thursday I had my kids in nineteen minutes, and my youngest said the kitty waved at her. I cried a little in the minivan." The school's regular crossing guard, out with a sprained ankle, has asked that the visitor return as his assistant.

Principal Dana Whitfield issued a statement thanking families for their patience and reminding everyone that only approved staff may direct traffic. Off the record, she admitted the ducks have never looked safer. Drive slow, stay in your lane, and wave at the crossing guard, whoever they are.

title: CATBOY BUILDS SIX-FOOT SNOW CAT DURING RARE CULLMAN FLURRY
headline: CATBOY BUILDS SIX-FOOT SNOW CAT DURING RARE CULLMAN FLURRY
summary: During Cullman's first measurable snowfall in four years, residents woke to find a six-foot snow cat sitting in the town square, and a doorbell camera clip showing Catboy adding the final whiskers just before dawn.
commentary:
In Alabama, half an inch of snow is a state of emergency. Bread vanishes, milk evaporates, and schools close at the mere rumor of flurries. So when Cullman woke Tuesday under a rare white dusting, residents were braced for chaos. They were not braced for a six-foot snow cat in the town square.

The sculpture was remarkably detailed: pointed ears, a tail wrapped neatly around its paws, and whiskers made of pine needles. Nearly every flake within a block had apparently been gathered to build it, leaving the surrounding sidewalks oddly bare. A neighbor's doorbell camera caught the sculptor at work just before 5 AM, tongue out in concentration, wearing red mittens borrowed from a nearby clothesline.

Retired shop teacher Harold Mize was the first to inspect it up close. "The proportions are perfect. The ears are a little big, but I think that's on purpose. If you ask me, he made it of himself and was just too modest to say so." Mize returned the mittens to the clothesline personally.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting a 9.0/10, adding bonus points for craftsmanship and deducting a tenth for the mitten loan. By noon, the sun had reduced the masterpiece to a puddle with two pine-needle whiskers floating in it. Bundle up, Cullman, and enjoy the snow while it lasts, because it never lasts.

title: CATBOY BARTERS PINECONE FOR PINT OF CREAM AT CHATTANOOGA FARMERS MARKET
headline: CATBOY BARTERS PINECONE FOR PINT OF CREAM AT CHATTANOOGA FARMERS MARKET
summary: A dairy vendor at a predawn farmers market in Chattanooga, Tennessee, accepted a single exceptionally nice pinecone in exchange for a pint of fresh cream from a shy customer with cat ears, and says it was the best deal she has made all season.
commentary:
Farmers markets run on trust, small talk, and cash in a cigar box. At the Riverside Saturday Market in Chattanooga, Tennessee, they now also run on pinecones. Shortly after 5 AM, while vendors were still unloading tables by headlamp, Catboy appeared at the Holler Hill Dairy stand holding something behind his back.

It was a pinecone. Not just any pinecone, according to witnesses, but a perfectly symmetrical, freshly fallen, beautifully open pinecone, the kind people spray gold and put on the mantel at Christmas. He set it on the counter, nudged it forward with one finger, and stared meaningfully at a glass pint of heavy cream.

Dairy farmer Opal Lindquist accepted the offer without hesitation. "I've had folks haggle me down on butter like it was a used car. He brought me the prettiest pinecone I've ever seen and looked at me with those big eyes. Honey, that's a fair trade in any economy." Catboy reportedly drank half the pint on the spot and strolled off wearing a cream mustache with total dignity.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the transaction a 7.6/10, noting that the pinecone joins the bottle cap as a confirmed form of Catboy currency. The pinecone now sits beside the Holler Hill cash box, and Lindquist says it is not for sale. Shop local, bring your own bags, and never underestimate a good pinecone.

title: CATBOY'S TAIL PUFFS TO TRIPLE SIZE WITH EVERY THUNDERCLAP IN DOTHAN STORM
headline: CATBOY'S TAIL PUFFS TO TRIPLE SIZE WITH EVERY THUNDERCLAP IN DOTHAN STORM
summary: A storm chaser outside Dothan filmed Catboy taking shelter on the porch of a closed general store during a violent lightning storm, his tail inflating dramatically with every boom until he finally curled up inside it like a sleeping bag.
commentary:
The Wiregrass knows a thing or two about thunderstorms. They come hot, loud, and often. But Friday night's storm over Dothan will be remembered not for its four thousand lightning strikes, but for the one fluffy tail that reacted to every single one of them.

Storm chaser Brenda Kilgore was filming from her truck outside Hatcher's General Store, closed for the night, when a flash revealed a figure huddled on the covered porch, knees pulled into an oversized hoodie. With every boom, his tail inflated. By the twentieth strike it was roughly the size of a beanbag chair, and his messy hair stood straight up with static that crackled visibly in the dark.

Kilgore was laughing as she described it. "I've chased storms for twenty years and I have never seen anything so scared look so cute. Every time it thundered, he'd jump, puff up, look around to see if anybody noticed, then act real casual. I know that move. My cat Biscuit does that move."

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the sighting a 9.4/10, calling it the most electrically significant Catboy event on record. Hatcher's owner found a round, fur-lined dent in the porch cushion the next morning. Unplug your electronics, stay away from tall things, and remember that nobody is too cool to be scared of thunder.

title: CATBOY ORDERS PLATE OF NOTHING BUT WHIPPED CREAM AT ALL-NIGHT BIRMINGHAM DINER
headline: CATBOY ORDERS PLATE OF NOTHING BUT WHIPPED CREAM AT ALL-NIGHT BIRMINGHAM DINER
summary: Staff at a 24-hour Birmingham diner say Catboy slid into a corner booth at 4:05 AM, pointed silently at the whipped cream canister, and ate an entire plate of it with the dignity of a food critic.
commentary:
The Starlite Diner on Highway 280 has served truckers, night nurses, and at least one wedding party still in costume. Until last week it had never served a cryptid. At 4:05 AM, the dining-room camera captured Catboy slipping into booth nine, hood up, ears poking through two suspiciously ear-shaped holes in the fabric.

He did not open the menu. He did not ask about the specials. He simply pointed at the whipped cream canister on the dessert cart and waited. June Pettibone, a twenty-two-year veteran of the graveyard shift, made an executive decision and built him a tower on a pancake plate, hold the pancakes.

"I've had grown men order pie at four in the morning and cry into it," Pettibone said. "This one licked the plate clean, tipped me with a shiny bottle cap, and slid out the door sideways like a cartoon. Best customer I had all week." The bottle cap is now taped above the register.

Dr. Patricia Meowton scored the event a 7.9/10 on the Weird-o-Meter, noting the bottle-cap tip as a promising sign of an emerging Catboy economy. The Starlite has since added a new item to its overnight menu, priced at one shiny object. Keep the coffee hot, the canisters full, and booth nine open.

title: CATBOY WARMS HANDS AT GAS STATION HOT DOG ROLLER FOR NEARLY AN HOUR
headline: CATBOY WARMS HANDS AT GAS STATION HOT DOG ROLLER FOR NEARLY AN HOUR
summary: Overnight cameras at a Hattiesburg gas station show Catboy hovering over the hot dog roller grill for fifty-three minutes, tracking each rotating frank with his eyes, before buying exactly one with a jar of pennies.
commentary:
Somewhere between midnight and sunrise, every gas station hot dog roller becomes a campfire for lost souls. At the Pine Belt Fuel Stop off Highway 49 in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, it became a hearth for a cryptid. Footage stamped 3:26 AM shows Catboy approaching the roller grill and holding out both palms like a weary traveler at a frontier stove.

For fifty-three minutes he stayed there, head swaying gently as each hot dog made its slow, eternal rotation. His pupils widened every time one rolled to the front. At one point he reached for the tongs, reconsidered, and went back to simply watching, as if the spinning itself were the meal.

Cashier Wendell Foy, nineteen, said the visitor finally approached the counter with a mason jar. "He counted out two dollars and nineteen cents in pennies, one at a time, real slow. I didn't rush him. You don't rush a man who's made his decision." Catboy left with one jumbo frank, no bun, and a single packet of relish he never opened.

Dr. Patricia Meowton rated the encounter a 6.8/10, calling it touching but well within known Catboy hunger patterns. Foy now keeps one frank warming at the back of the roller every night, marked reserved. Fill up, warm up, and pay in exact change when you can.
